the impact of government regulations on the continuance intention of consumers to adopt in store proximity mobile payments.
the effects of perceived demonetisation regulations on the continuance usage of proximity mobile payment service.
the effects of moral obligation, merchant pro actives and perceived regulation on continuance intention.

the TPB-NAM integrated model could be used to predict continuance intention of mobile payment usage.
the government regulation (d. e. demonetisation) has a significant effect on the continuance intention of mobile payment service.
the government regulation of demonetisation has a significant effect on the continuance usage of proximity mobile payment service in India.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TPB model can be enhanced to better explain the continuance usage of proximity mobile payment after government regulation.
the TPB model can be extended with NAM and government regulation as moderator to explain the determinants of mobile payment services.
the TPB model could not sufficiently explain the continuance intention of the users of mobile payment services.

the government can use the TPB model to design and formulate more effective policies to regulate mobile payment services.

perceived government regulation (i.e. demonetisation) can have a significant influence on the usage intention of in store mobile payment services, which can be used as a guide for the government and other policymakers to outline more reasonable mandatory regulation policies.
